problem: Let $T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}-2x+y \\ -x+4y \\ -3x-5y\end{aligned}]$ be a linear transformation. Determine the value of $k$ for which the vector $v=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -4 \\ k\end{aligned}]$ belongs to $\text{Im}(T).$

examples.worked_solution:
The vector $\mathbf{v}$ belongs to $\textrm{Im}(\mathbf{T})$ if there exists a vector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14071327/assets/be82bf02cdfe6a50557b312ba78708463248f844f81016df2cda41c6cfbb6c1a.png) such that $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{u}) = \mathbf{v}.$ 

Therefore, we must have

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x+y \\ -x+y \\ 2y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ k \\ 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+y=4 \\ -x+y=k \\ 2y=8.\end{aligned}
$$

From the third equation, we get $y=4,$ which we substitute into the first equation to get 

$$
\begin{aligned}x+y & =4 \\ x+4 & =4 \\ x & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $x=0$ and $y=4$ into the third equation and obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-x+y & =k \\ 0+4 & =k \\ k & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\mathbf{v}\in\textrm{Im}(\mathbf{T})$ when $k=4.$
